slot.brief: Find the energy (or wavelength) of the photon emitted when an electron in a hydrogen-like ion jumps from n=2 to n=1.

stem: For the transition $n=2$ to $n=1$, hydrogen emits a photon of wavelength $121.6$ nm. What is the wavelength emitted in the same transition by a hydrogen-like $\text{He}^+$ ion?

verdicts.working: For a hydrogen-like ion, the transition energy scales as Z², so the wavelength scales as 1/Z². For He⁺, λ = 121.6/4 = 30.4 nm.

working:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\propto Z^2\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2}-\dfrac{1}{2^2}\right)$ for this transition.
$\lambda_{\text{He}^+}=\dfrac{\lambda_{\text{H}}}{2^2}=\dfrac{121.6}{4}\text{ nm}=30.4\text{ nm}$

Independent check: For a hydrogen-like ion, the transition energy scales as Z², so the wavelength scales as 1/Z². For He⁺, λ = 121.6/4 = 30.4 nm.
solution:
For the same transition, $1/\lambda \propto Z^2$, so wavelength scales as $1/Z^2$. For He$^+$, $Z=2$:
$$\lambda_{\text{He}^+}=\frac{121.6}{2^2}\text{ nm}=30.4\text{ nm}$$
